_README: The official government page each PDF in this directory came from.
A citation under an answer shows the document it was drawn from. Without a
URL that is a filename, which nobody can follow. With one it becomes a link
to the government's own page, which is what someone actually needs when
they want to read the rule themselves or take it to an office.
Filled in by hand, on purpose. This codebase never constructs a URL:
services/websearch.py consults no model at all so that it cannot invent
one, and tests/test_official_url.py asserts the assistant never assembles
one either. A guessed address looks exactly as official as a real one and
sends a person somewhere wrong. So an entry left empty is correct and safe
-- the citation falls back to naming the document, as it does today.
Paste the address you downloaded the PDF from. It is not required to point
at the PDF itself; the scheme's own page is usually more useful to a person
